title: Morgan Hill 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Morgan Hill 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Morgan Hill 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Morgan Hill's Cochrane Road manufacturing parks, downtown Monterey Road retail, and owner-user flex buildings.

sections.html: Morgan Hill sits between the dense build-out of San Jose and the agricultural land around Gilroy, and its commercial base reflects that middle position with precision manufacturing and business park flex space near Cochrane Road alongside a small downtown retail strip on Monterey Road. Much of the manufacturing product here serves owner-users, companies buying their own building rather than leasing, which shifts the underwriting conversation for a 1031 exchanger away from tenant credit and toward the building's suitability for the buyer's own operation. Morgan Hill's population has grown steadily over recent decades without ever taking on the density of San Jose to its north, and that slower, more deliberate growth pattern has kept much of the town's manufacturing base owner-occupied rather than turning over to institutional landlords the way larger industrial parks elsewhere in the county have.

sections.heading: Light Industrial and Precision Manufacturing Near Cochrane Road
sections.html: The business parks along Cochrane Road and Condit Road house precision manufacturing and light assembly tenants, many of them smaller companies supplying larger Silicon Valley technology firms rather than end consumers directly. Building specifications in this corridor vary more than in a typical warehouse market, since precision manufacturing tenants often need specialized power capacity, cleanroom space, or vibration control that an ordinary industrial building does not provide. A replacement property buyer should confirm which of these specialized features, if any, the current tenant actually requires before assuming the building's rent supports a broader industrial tenant base. A building outfitted heavily for one tenant's specialized process can be harder to re-lease to a general industrial user at the same rent if that tenant ever moves on, so a buyer should factor re-tenanting cost into the underwriting rather than treating the specialized build-out as pure upside.

sections.heading: Downtown Monterey Road Retail and Restaurant Space
sections.html: Monterey Road carries Morgan Hill's small downtown retail and restaurant corridor, serving both local residents and visitors drawn to the surrounding wine country foothills. Lease terms here run shorter and rents lower than the manufacturing product near Cochrane Road, and a buyer should not expect the same underwriting approach to transfer between the two very different parts of Morgan Hill's commercial base.

sections.heading: Business Park Flex Space Serving Smaller Manufacturers
sections.html:
Flex buildings in Morgan Hill's business parks split office and industrial space within the same footprint, letting smaller manufacturers house both their production floor and administrative staff under one roof. A diligence file for a Morgan Hill flex or manufacturing property typically includes:

  • Power capacity and any specialized infrastructure documentation
  • Confirmation of owner-user versus leased-tenant occupancy
  • Zoning verification for manufacturing use classification
  • Lease term and rent roll for multi-tenant flex buildings
  • Seismic retrofit records for any pre-1990s construction
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

An owner-user buyer should confirm the zoning classification supports the intended manufacturing use specifically, rather than a general industrial designation that may carry restrictions the buyer has not anticipated. Loading dock configuration and yard space also vary meaningfully between Morgan Hill's older business park buildings and its newer construction, and a buyer should confirm the specific building matches the equipment and vehicle access the operation actually requires.

sections.heading: Three-Property Rule Strategy for Single-Building Exchanges
sections.html: Many Morgan Hill exchanges involve an owner-user moving from one manufacturing building into another rather than trading between different asset classes, and the three-property rule tends to fit this pattern well, letting the buyer name a primary candidate along with one or two backups if a specific building does not clear zoning or power-capacity diligence. Each identified property should still list a specific address rather than a general description of an acceptable building type.

sections.heading: Lender Preflight for Owner-User Manufacturing Buyers
sections.html: An owner-user buyer financing a Morgan Hill manufacturing building should bring the lender into the process early, since underwriting an owner-occupied industrial purchase differs from underwriting a leased investment property, and the lender may require operating financials from the buyer's business rather than relying solely on the real estate itself. This content describes process and coordination only; a buyer should confirm gain treatment and depreciation recapture with a tax advisor before the exchange agreement is signed.

faqs.q: Why does Morgan Hill have so much owner-user manufacturing property?
faqs.a: The business parks near Cochrane and Condit Roads house many smaller precision manufacturing companies that buy their own buildings rather than lease, which shifts underwriting toward the building's suitability for the buyer's operation rather than tenant credit.

faqs.q: What specialized features should I check on a Cochrane Road manufacturing building?
faqs.a: Confirm power capacity, cleanroom space, or vibration control needs specific to the current or intended tenant, since precision manufacturing buildings vary more in these specifications than a typical warehouse.

faqs.q: Does Monterey Road retail underwrite the same way as Cochrane Road manufacturing?
faqs.a: No. Monterey Road carries shorter lease terms and lower rents tied to local retail and restaurant demand, a different profile from the manufacturing and flex product near the business parks.

faqs.q: Why use the three-property rule for a Morgan Hill owner-user exchange?
faqs.a: Many of these exchanges involve moving between manufacturing buildings of a similar type, and naming a primary candidate plus one or two backups under the three-property rule provides a fallback if zoning or power-capacity diligence rules one out.

faqs.q: What should an owner-user buyer tell the lender early in the process?
faqs.a: Flag that the purchase is owner-occupied rather than a leased investment property, since the lender may need operating financials from the buyer's business in addition to the real estate itself.
